findings.title: Reward as enduring provision
findings.claim: In 5:85, the reward is pictured as an inhabited environment whose water and benefit continue to run.
findings.mechanism: The focus garden and river nouns meet the ongoing flow verb, while the recompense term supplies the returned-benefit frame; together they make the reward a sustaining habitat rather than an unpictured award.
findings.reader_payoff: The rivers become part of what the reward does: they depict provision continuing within the protected garden spaces.
findings.containment: This is a local environmental reading of the focus wording. It does not name a surah-wide water system or claim that the focus literally transforms another image into rivers.

epistemic.reason: The focus branches and the channel supports are trusted and directly anchored, while the integration of flow into continuing provision is a bounded macro inference.

findings.title: Reward answers requested standing
findings.claim: The reward scene can also be read as the immediate completion of the speakers' request for recognized membership: the garden is the destination, and the good-doer class ratifies their standing.
findings.mechanism: The preceding context asks to be registered with witnesses and admitted among a sound community; the focus then answers with gardens and names the result as the recompense of good-doers. The relation is supplied by an attributed HFT trace whose exact context coordinates land on the focus words.
findings.reader_payoff: The answer in 5:85 becomes socially legible as well as spatial: the speakers receive a place and a recognized company.
findings.containment: The garden reward remains an individual benefit in the plain reading. This attributed overlay says the sequence also narratively answers a request for affiliation; it does not claim that the packet limits all garden reward to group membership.

epistemic.reason: All anchors and word coordinates are supplied and complete, but the source is legacy_unbound and five context branch records have no independent registry gloss, so the reading remains explicitly attributed.

findings.title: Abiding as settled attachment
findings.claim: The focus's abiding condition can also be perceived as attachment to the condition that conduct brings back, with the pericope placing the same abiding form in an adverse setting.
findings.mechanism: The focus joins returned recompense to abiding in gardens, while 5:80 places affiliation, what the selves send forward, displeasure, and abiding in punishment. The attributed attachment branch makes permanence register as settled relation as well as duration.
findings.reader_payoff: The contrast between the two abiding environments becomes relational: conduct and orientation lead into the condition to which the people remain attached.
findings.containment: Duration remains the recoverable primary sense of the focus participle. The attached-condition reading is an attributed contextual addition and does not claim that permanence is only spatial or relational.

epistemic.reason: The exact 5:80 and 5:85 coordinates and focus branch records support the comparison, but the HFT source is legacy_unbound and three traced context branches remain registry-unresolved.

epistemic.reason: The exact 5:83 and 5:85 surfaces and coordinates anchor the water-motion contact, but the HFT source is legacy_unbound and the record itself limits the relation to imagistic amplification.

findings.title: External judgment horizon
findings.claim: The explicitly added 1:4 frame can make the focus recompense perceptible as positive return within an accountable judgment horizon.
findings.mechanism: The focus noun جَزَاءُ names an action-matched return, while the external occurrence 1:4:3 supplies the الحساب والجزاء cue of الدِّين; their contact adds an eschatological accountability frame to the already present reward.
findings.reader_payoff: The reward is newly seen as a recompense situated within judgment, not only as a benefit described in isolation.
findings.containment: The overlay does not claim that 5:85 itself states a day or import the whole of Fātiḥa. It adds only the judgment-horizon relation through 1:4:3.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus occurrence and external context occurrence/root cue are supplied, but no support_registry trust label attaches to this independently authored overlay relation.

findings.title: External favor beside earned good
findings.claim: The explicitly added 1:7 frame places the focus's good-doer designation beside bestowed favor, so the recompense can remain a response to action while also being perceived in a grace-facing relation.
findings.mechanism: The focus active participle names enacted good action, and its supplied extension allows goodness to exceed an exact return; the external occurrence 1:7:3 names those who have been favored. The contact adds received favor without collapsing it into the action-based class.
findings.reader_payoff: The closing class of good-doers carries both an ethical identity and a newly visible relation to favor received.
findings.containment: The overlay does not equate good-doers with every favored person or claim that recompense is unearned. It adds a bounded favor comparison through 1:7:3 only.

epistemic.reason: The focus hsn facets and exact external favor occurrence are supplied, while the cross-ayah grace relation is an independently authored, bounded inference without a support_registry trust label.
